claims.claim: SemiAnalysis describes more than 24 gigawatts of data centres in advanced construction across 40 campuses, most more than halfway done, to be delivered in 2027.
claims.episode_span: more than 24 gigawatts of data centres in an advanced stage of construction, across 40 campuses
claims.source_title: Datacenters 2027: The Year of Acceleration, +50GW in a Single Year
claims.supporting_quote: one picture, >24GW of datacenters in advanced stage of construction, all to be delivered in 2027. Most of them are more than halfway done, with exterior cooling and electrical equipment already installed. Thats just 40 campuses

claims.claim: Slightly under 1 trillion dollars of binding, non-cancellable data-centre leases have been signed year to date.

claims.episode_span: A typical contract runs 15 to 20 years, with a total contract value of 30 to 50 billion dollars per gigawatt
claims.source_title: Datacenters 2027: The Year of Acceleration, +50GW in a Single Year
claims.supporting_quote: developers typically only spend 5-10% of project capital without a customer. They need a pre-lease to fund and develop the whole project. Thats typically a 15-20 year contract, with a TCV of $30-50B per GW.

claims.claim: Brad Gerstner said a plus-43-gigawatt 2027 forecast was too aggressive and that he thought only about 25 gigawatts would be built.
claims.episode_span: a plus-43-gigawatt 2027 forecast that Altimeter’s Brad Gerstner called too aggressive against his own figure of about 25 gigawatts
claims.source_title: Datacenters 2027: The Year of Acceleration, +50GW in a Single Year
claims.supporting_quote: Brad Gerstner from Altimeter showed our data on the All-In Podcast and stated that SemiAnalysis forecast of +43GW in 2027 is too aggressive and that he thought only about 25GW would get built

claims.claim: The piece treats about 50 gigawatts in 2027 as equivalent to the global cumulative data-centre market through 2024 built in one year.

claims.source_title: Datacenters 2027: The Year of Acceleration, +50GW in a Single Year
claims.supporting_quote: +50GW is essentially the global cumulative datacenter market up through 2024 being built in one year!

claims.claim: Industry estimates put next year’s HBM demand at about 61.5 billion gigabits, up 91 percent, against possible shipments of 54.6 billion gigabits, about a 10 percent gap.
claims.episode_span: high-bandwidth memory demand next year is about 61.5 billion gigabits, up 91 percent from this year, while memory makers may ship only 54.6 billion gigabits
claims.source_title: Samsung Works with TSMC on Nvidia’s Custom HBM
claims.supporting_quote: The industry expects HBM demand to hit about 61.5 billion gigabits next year, up 91% from this year. However, memory makers may ship only 54.6 billion gigabits, creating about a 10% supply gap.

claims.claim: TSMC’s 3-nanometer yield is estimated above 90 percent, compared with about 60 percent for Samsung’s SF2 process, and NVHBM’s physical layer is 60 percent smaller than standard HBM.
claims.episode_span: TSMC’s 3-nanometer yield is estimated above 90 percent against about 60 percent for Samsung’s comparable 2-nanometer SF2 process
claims.source_title: Samsung Works with TSMC on Nvidia’s Custom HBM
claims.supporting_quote: The industry estimates its yield at over 90%. In comparison, Samsung’s comparable 2nm SF2 process reportedly sits at around 60%.

claims.claim: NVHBM can deliver up to 30 percent more memory bandwidth and 15 percent lower power than standard HBM4E, and Nvidia wants the core die on 1c DRAM.
claims.episode_span: NVHBM can deliver up to 30 percent more memory bandwidth and 15 percent lower power than standard HBM4E
claims.source_title: Samsung Reportedly Taps TSMC for Nvidia's Next-Gen Memory
claims.supporting_quote: Nvidia unveiled NVHBM, a custom design that integrates the memory controller into the base die and can deliver up to 30% more memory bandwidth and 15% lower power consumption than standard HBM4E.

claims.claim: The GlobalFoundries-TSMC interposer deal is valued at 2 billion dollars over five years, with capacity expansion in Malta, New York.

claims.supporting_quote: The deal, valued at $2 billion (£1.5bn) over five years, means that TSMC customers will be able to market products as having been entirely manufactured and packaged within the US.
